messages:
jane: Hey folks — after upgrading the redwood Python package from 1.1.4 -> 1.2.0 our web app crashes at startup with an ImportError. Happening in prod after a deploy. stacktrace below. Can someone help?

jane: ```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"/srv/app/app.py\", line 3, in <module>
    from redwood import CompletionClient
ImportError: cannot import name 'CompletionClient' from 'redwood' (/srv/app/current/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/redwood/__init__.py)
```

alex: thanks for the report — a few quick checks: which install tool are you using (pip vs poetry), do you have extras, and can you paste `python -c \"import redwood, sys; print(redwood.__file__, getattr(redwood, '__version__', 'no-version'))\"` output? Also any local packages named `redwood` in the repo?

jane: we use poetry. I ran `poetry add redwood==1.2.0` then `poetry install`. We do use the `aio` extras for async helpers: `redwood[aio]`. I ran the python check and got: `/srv/app/current/src/redwood/__init__.py no-version` (so __version__ is missing?). That path seems odd — our package layout has src/ because we use Poetry with packages = [{ include = \"app\" }]... Not sure why src/redwood exists.

alex: that path is suspicious — it looks like there's a local package in your repo (src/redwood) shadowing the installed wheel. Common when people have a top-level folder or editable install. Can you run `pip show redwood` and `python -c \"import importlib, pkgutil; print(importlib.import_module('redwood').__file__); print(list(pkgutil.iter_modules(['src'])))\"` and paste results?

jane: output: `pip show redwood` -> "Name: redwood\nVersion: 1.2.0\nLocation: /srv/app/current/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages". The second command prints `/srv/app/current/src/redwood/__init__.py` and `ModuleInfo(name='redwood', ispkg=True)`.

alex: yep — you have a local package named `redwood` in `src/` (probably from an earlier internal library or a folder created during testing). Python's import system prefers your project source path over site-packages at runtime (depending on sys.path), so the import resolves to your local package which doesn't implement the new API, hence ImportError.

chris: other things to check quickly: 1) editable installs (pip install -e .) won't include extras unless specified; 2) lockfile constraining redwood version to older one; 3) ensure your build step doesn't copy a `src/redwood` directory into the image.

jane: aha — our CI Dockerfile does `COPY . /srv/app/current` and then installs dependencies in venv. That COPY includes `src/redwood` and it ends up shadowing the wheel. Locally i didn't catch it because I had editable dev env.

alex: fix options (pick one):
- rename the local folder (`src/redwood`) to avoid the name collision (recommended).
- adjust PYTHONPATH/sys.path in your container so site-packages are before the project src (not ideal).
- remove the stray `src/redwood` from the repo if it's not used.
- as a quick workaround, in your app entrypoint do: `import pkgutil, importlib; importlib.invalidate_caches();` then `from importlib import import_module; print(import_module('redwood').__file__)` to verify.

jane: renaming the folder fixed the startup import error in staging. But I still got a runtime error where `redwood.CompletionClient` exists in 1.2.0 but our code uses an older client name. I had mixed versions in the codebase and tests. I updated imports to the new API and pinned `redwood==1.2.0` in pyproject.

chris: about the extras you mentioned (`redwood[aio]`) — note that installing from source with `pip install -e .` requires you to include extras in the install command (`pip install -e .[aio]`) or declare extras in the project metadata. Poetry should handle extras when you `poetry add redwood[aio]`, but editable/local path installs behave differently. If you see missing async helpers, run `pip install 'redwood[aio]==1.2.0'` inside the venv to be safe.

jane: did that — `pip install 'redwood[aio]==1.2.0'` and now the async helpers are available. Staging looks good, pushing to prod now. Thanks. :tada:

alex: glad it's resolved. We'll add a short KB entry for "ImportError after SDK upgrade due to local package shadowing" with repro steps and the `python -c` checks.

dev-deploy-bot: deploy finished for service web-api (sha: abc123) — success :white_check_mark:

jane: confirmed prod is healthy. Closing.

chris: marking support ticket #7891 resolved and adding note about extras vs editable installs to docs.
